summary: The mizbeach makes holy what is fit for it, so a pasul thing that went up on it does not come down. Rabbi Yehoshua says this is for things fit for the fire, and Rabban Gamliel says for anything fit for the mizbeach, even blood and nesachim.
stIntro: Certain unfit items, once they have been placed on the altar, are nevertheless sacrificed.

chunks.en: The mizbeach makes holy what is fit for it.
chunks.st: The mishna teaches: The altar sanctifies only items that are suited to it.
chunks.stMore: The tanna’im disagree as to the definition of suited for the altar.

summary: These animals were already pasul before they came to the Beis HaMikdash, so they come down even if they went up on the mizbeach. Rabbi Akiva says blemished animals do not come down.

chunks.en: These did not become pasul in the holy place:
chunks.st: And these are the offerings whose disqualification did not occur in sanctity:

chunks.en: animals used in a forbidden act,
chunks.st: An animal that copulated with a person, and an animal that was the object of bestiality,

summary: Just as these things do not come down once they went up, they do not go back up once they came down. An animal that went up alive must come down, but if it was shechted on top of the mizbeach, it is skinned and cut up there.

chunks.en: Just as if they went up they do not come down,
chunks.st: Concerning those animals that, if they ascended, do not descend, just as if they ascended the altar they shall not descend,

chunks.en: so too if they came down they do not go up.
chunks.st: so too, if they descended they shall not then ascend.

chunks.en: And all of them that went up alive to the top of the mizbeach
chunks.st: And all of them that if they ascend they do not descend, if they ascended to the top of the altar alive

chunks.he: יֵרֵדוּ. עוֹלָה שֶׁעָלְתָה חַיָּה לְרֹאשׁ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
chunks.en: come down. An olah that went up alive to the top of the mizbeach
chunks.st: they descend, as an animal is fit for the altar only after it is slaughtered. A burnt offering that ascended to the top of the altar alive

chunks.en: comes down. If he shechted it on top of the mizbeach,
chunks.st: shall descend, as one does not slaughter an animal atop the altar ab initio. But if one slaughtered the animal at the top of the altar,

chunks.en: he should skin it and cut it up in its place.
chunks.st: he should flay it and cut it into pieces in its place, and it is not removed from the altar.

summary: Things that are not for the mizbeach, like meat for eating, the lechem hapanim, and the leftover menachos, must come down even if they went up. Wool, hair, bones and horns go up while attached to the korban, but not once they came off.

chunks.en: And these, if they went up, come down:
chunks.st: And these are the items that if they ascended upon the altar they descend, because they are completely unfit for the altar:

chunks.en: the meat of the holiest korbanos,
chunks.st: The meat of offerings of the most sacred order,
chunks.stMore: i.e., a guilt offering and a sin offering, the meat of which is eaten by priests;

chunks.en: and the meat of less holy korbanos,
chunks.st: and the meat of offerings of lesser sanctity, which is eaten by the owners;

chunks.en: and the leftover of the omer,
chunks.st: and the surplus of the omer
chunks.stMore: meal offering brought on the second day of Passover after the handful was removed and burned on the altar;

words.note: A mincha of barley brought on the second day of Pesach.

chunks.en: and the two loaves,
chunks.st: and the two loaves meal offering brought on the festival of Shavuot;

chunks.en: and the lechem hapanim,
chunks.st: and the shewbread;

summary: Pasul things or coals that fell off the mizbeach are not put back. Parts of a kosher olah that fell off before midnight are put back, and using them is me'ilah; after midnight they are not put back.

chunks.en: And all of them that fell off the top of the mizbeach,
chunks.st: And all of those disqualified offerings with regard to which it was taught (84a) that if they ascended they do not descend, in a case where they were dislodged from upon the altar,

chunks.en: he should not put them back.
chunks.st: the priest does not restore them to the altar.

chunks.he: וְכֵן גַּחֶלֶת שֶׁפָּקְעָה מֵעַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
chunks.en: And so too a coal that fell off the top of the mizbeach.
chunks.st: And likewise, with regard to an ember that was dislodged from upon the altar, the priest does not restore it to the altar.

chunks.en: Parts that fell off the top of the mizbeach,
chunks.st: As for limbs of a fit burnt offering that were dislodged from upon the altar,

chunks.en: before midnight,
chunks.st: if they were dislodged before midnight,

chunks.en: he should put them back, and using them is me'ilah.
chunks.st: the priest should restore them to the altar and one is liable for misusing them.

chunks.en: After midnight,
chunks.st: But if they were dislodged after midnight,

chunks.en: he should not put them back,
chunks.st: the priest does not restore them

chunks.en: and using them is not me'ilah.
chunks.st: and one is not liable for misusing them,
chunks.stMore: as one is not liable for misuse of consecrated property after it has fulfilled the purpose for which it was designated.

summary: Just as the mizbeach makes holy what is fit for it, so do the ramp and the holy vessels. Vessels for liquids make liquids holy, and measures for dry things make dry things holy, but only in the courtyard.

chunks.en: Just as the mizbeach makes holy what is fit
chunks.st: With regard to unfit items that if they ascended do not descend, just as the altar sanctifies

chunks.en: for it, so too the ramp makes holy.
chunks.st: items that are suited to it, so too, the ramp sanctifies items that are suited to it.

chunks.en: Just as the mizbeach and the ramp make holy
chunks.st: Just as the altar and the ramp sanctify

chunks.en: what is fit for them,
chunks.st: items that are suited to them,

chunks.en: so too the vessels make holy.
chunks.st: so too, the service vessels sanctify
chunks.stMore: items that are placed in them. The mishna elaborates on the halakha taught in the previous mishna (86a) that service vessels sanctify items placed in them.

words.note: The holy vessels of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: Vessels for liquids make liquids holy,
chunks.st: The service vessels used for liquids sanctify only liquids used in the service,

chunks.en: and measures for dry things make dry things holy.
chunks.st: and the service vessels that serve as dry measures sanctify only dry items used in the service.

chunks.he: אֵין כְּלֵי הַלַּח מְקַדְּשִׁים אֶת הַיָּבֵשׁ,
chunks.en: Vessels for liquids do not make dry things holy,
chunks.st: The service vessels used for liquids do not sanctify dry items,

chunks.he: וְלֹא מִדּוֹת הַיָּבֵשׁ מְקַדְּשׁוֹת אֶת הַלָּח.
chunks.en: and measures for dry things do not make liquids holy.
chunks.st: and the service vessels used for dry items do not sanctify liquids.

chunks.en: Holy vessels that got a hole,
chunks.st: With regard to sacred vessels that were perforated,

chunks.en: if they can still do the kind of job
chunks.st: if one continues to utilize them for a use similar to the use

chunks.en: they did when they were whole,
chunks.st: for which they would utilize them previously when they were whole, they

chunks.en: they make holy. And if not,
chunks.st: continue to sanctify their contents. And if not,

chunks.en: they do not make holy.
chunks.st: they do not sanctify their contents.

chunks.en: And all of them make holy only in the holy place.
chunks.st: And all of these vessels sanctify items only when they are in the sacred area, i.e., the Temple courtyard.
